test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 29 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Had you been / working regularly, / you had completed / the project yesterday.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"had"** is used as the past tense of 'have' to indicate possession or a past action. However, in conditional sentences, it is paired with the past perfect form.

 
 
• **Example: **They** had **finished the work before the deadline.
 
 
 
• **"would have"** is used in the past conditional tense to indicate an action that would have happened if a certain condition had been met. (होगा)
 
 
• **Example: **If you had called me, I **would have** come.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct phrase should be "you would have completed" instead of "you had completed".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Had you been** (क्या तुम होते): This phrase is correctly used in the past perfect continuous tense.

 
 
• **Example:** Had you been more careful, the accident would have been avoided.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: the project yesterday** (प्रोजेक्ट कल): This phrase correctly indicates the timing of the project completion.
 
 
• **Example:** I submitted the project yesterday.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: working regularly** (नियमित रूप से काम कर रहे): This phrase correctly shows the continuous action.
 
 
• **Example:** She has been working regularly on her fitness goals.
